title: Google Cloud Announces Strategic Partnership with Verizon to Scale Enterprise AI - HPCwire
description: Google Cloud Announces Strategic Partnership with Verizon to Scale Enterprise AI HPCwire
bottomLine: Google-Verizon partnership scales enterprise AI delivery—signals consolidation of cloud, telecom, and AI—threatens independent research platforms.
keyFindings: Google Cloud and Verizon announce strategic partnership to scale enterprise AI infrastructure and deployment.
Verizon's telecom and edge computing footprint combined with Google's AI/cloud creates integrated offering.
Partnership targets enterprise customers seeking reliable, distributed AI infrastructure.
Represents major cloud provider consolidation that could marginalize smaller, specialized platforms.
whyItMatters: Dutch enterprise research institutions and corporate R&D labs increasingly source AI services through integrated telecom-cloud-AI bundles. Elsevier must position ScienceDirect/Scopus/LeapSpace as independent, specialized research intelligence that remains neutral and not locked into any single cloud vendor's ecosystem—crucial for institutions valuing research freedom and data sovereignty.
actionItems: Audit Elsevier's cloud dependencies—ensure messaging emphasizes platform independence and interoperability.
Create 'research neutrality' positioning for Dutch institutions wary of vendor lock-in via Google-Verizon bundle.
Identify Dutch telecom/enterprise customers using both Verizon and research tools—pitch Elsevier as anti-lock-in alternative.

title: Open Science NL launches 2026-2027 work programme with a dedicated AI and Open Science funding track
description: Open Science NL's new 2026-2027 work programme is structured around five themes (Infrastructure, Capacity building, Empowering communities, Incentives, Monitoring and evaluation), including a new 'AI and Open Science' programme under Capacity building. The prior 2024-2025 programme funded projects worth €60 million across 15 instruments, nearly all now funded or implemented.
elsevierRelevance: A national funding body is putting dedicated money behind 'AI and Open Science' capacity-building — worth watching for what infrastructure and tools it ends up funding, since a prior programme already deployed €60M and this is the successor track.

title: Dutch research evaluation frameworks shift toward open research information, away from closed bibliometrics
description: Both the new Strategy Evaluation Protocol (SEP 2027-2033, published by UNL/NWO/KNAW) and NWO's evidence-based CV are moving toward assessment indicators based on open research information rather than closed, proprietary databases, implementing the Barcelona Declaration on Open Research Information. 16 Dutch research organisations have signed the Declaration since its 2024 launch. The change embeds openness directly into how research units and individual researchers are evaluated nationally.
elsevierRelevance: National research-evaluation frameworks moving away from closed, proprietary bibliometric indicators is a structural, multi-year threat to Scopus's role as the trusted metrics source Dutch institutions are evaluated against — the same policy current behind the Maastricht Scopus cancellation and the Web of Science exits.

title: Dutch research institutions and Elsevier announce new agreements
description: UNL, NFU, NWO-i, KNAW, 23 universities of applied science and Elsevier have signed new reading, publishing and Scopus agreements covering 66 Dutch research organisations, running from 1 January 2025 for two years with an optional third-year extension (through 2026, possibly 2027). The Read & Publish deal keeps ScienceDirect reading rights and adds 100% open access publishing in eligible journals; a separate agreement covers Scopus access. UNL's Anton Pijpers noted higher-education budget cuts are 'putting pressure on these types of agreements.'
elsevierRelevance: This is Elsevier's own core Dutch business relationship — the national Read & Publish and Scopus agreement covering all 66 major NL research organisations — with UNL's own spokesperson flagging budget pressure on renewal, directly relevant against the backdrop of Maastricht and others already cutting other subscription databases.

title: Dutch universities drop Web of Science as costs rise and open-science pressure builds
description: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Utrecht University, University of Twente, and University of Groningen/UMCG are all terminating their Clarivate Web of Science licenses (VU/Utrecht/Twente from 1 January 2026, Groningen/UMCG from 1 January 2027). VU cited two reasons: its Barcelona Declaration on Open Research Information commitment, and cost — renewal was expected to exceed €100,000 amid budget cuts. VU is directing researchers toward Scopus, OpenAIRE and OpenAlex as replacements, explicitly keeping its Scopus license in place.
elsevierRelevance: A four-university wave of subscription-database cancellations shows real budget and open-science pressure on paid citation databases generally — the same pressure that led Maastricht to drop Scopus. Notably VU is keeping Scopus while dropping Web of Science, a relative win for Elsevier over Clarivate specifically, worth tracking as other universities decide.

title: Maastricht University cancels Scopus license, invests in OpenAlex instead
description: Maastricht University Library is cancelling its Scopus license — Elsevier's abstract and citation database — effective 1 January 2027, citing declining usage, sharply rising costs, and diminishing unique content versus open alternatives. It is simultaneously entering a partner subscription with OpenAlex, the free open database, which will take over Scopus's supplementary role feeding UM's Current Research Information System (Pure). UM's separate license for full-text Elsevier journal access is unaffected.
elsevierRelevance: A named Dutch institution is dropping Elsevier's own Scopus product for a free open alternative — a direct, quantified competitive loss (cost and declining usage cited explicitly), not just a Clarivate/Web of Science story.
